adaptations.description: OneLineage's own changes on top of the vendored ios-sweet prefix. Each one is derived from the patched source, not guessed: they parameterise the constants that were hardcoded for the phone panel and give the platform expert an identity this project controls.

patches.name: 0001-onelineage-early-console-parameters.patch
patches.purpose: console: move the bootstrap console address, panel geometry and block attributes into SWEET.h so start.s, arm_vm_init and sweet_early.c cannot disagree

patches.name: 0002-onelineage-pl011-early-console.patch
patches.purpose: console: PL011 backend for SWEET_QEMU_PROFILE, mapped Device-nGnRnE, with the panel band and pixel path compiled out

patches.name: 0003-onelineage-platform-expert-identity.patch
patches.purpose: platform expert: match the 'onelineage,platform' compatible this project's ADT always publishes instead of one board's vendor strings

patches.name: 0004-onelineage-sweet-profile-flags.patch
patches.purpose: build: SWEET_PROFILE_FLAGS hook so a QEMU build adds -DSWEET_QEMU_PROFILE without a second machine config

notes: The series stops before ios-sweet's filesystem, AMFI, USB, input, display and SMP work; those are later milestones.
A clean apply proves text-level composition against the pinned tag only. It says nothing about compiling, linking, booting, or the phone.
The platform expert matches 'onelineage,platform' after 0003; mk_m3q_adt.py publishes it in the ADT root node, and a test keeps the two in agreement.
A QEMU build must pass SWEET_PROFILE_FLAGS=-DSWEET_QEMU_PROFILE, otherwise the kernel is the phone configuration and writes its bootstrap console to panel MMIO that QEMU does not have.
